subject: Post-call: Crestline discovery — model scorecard & next steps
messages:
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>

Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 Jul 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: Crestline discovery — model scorecard & next steps

Thanks again for the call this morning, Julian — good conversation and appreciate the clarity on the end-user examples (multi-field medical summaries + policy extraction). Quick recap and recommended next steps below so we have an actionable plan heading into the evals.

Recap (short):
- Primary goal: reliable structured extraction into a JSON customer schema (fields: diagnosis_codes, summary, flags) with <3% fmt/regression on schema compliance over 1000 test cases.
- Throughput/latency need: 300 TPS peak, P95 latency target ~250ms (initially on Redwood Dedicated).
- Security: Crestline requires KMS-backed key management and audit logs; LegalOps requested a SOC 2 artifact early in procurement.

Model scorecard (initial recommendations):
1) Llama-3-13B-chat (recommended) — best balance of instruction-following and cost for structured outputs; use 8-bit quantized variant for Dedicated.
2) Mistral-Instruct-7B (fallback) — lower cost, good for short fields; may need prompt engineering for complex extraction.
3) Small deterministic path (7B quantized with more aggressive temperature scheduling) for high-throughput stages of pipeline.

Benchmarks + assets attached:
- benchmark_summary_q3.csv — quick token cost / p95 latency estimate from our hosted runs against a 200-sample test set.
- crestline_prompt_set_v1.json — seed prompts and negative examples you gave on the call.
- schema_customer_response_v1.json — canonical JSON schema we're targeting for the eval.

Functional requirements & tool-calling notes:
- We recommend using structured output "function-like" calls: Redwood's structured output mode + JSON schema validation on the service side to fail fast.
- Retry policy: idempotency-token + exponential backoff (initial 200ms, multiplier 2, max 5s), and a deterministic fallback to the Mistral-Instruct-7B model for any schema failures above a soft threshold (10% on a rolling window).
- KV cache prefixing: for multi-turn patient notes, enable prefix caching to reduce token cost and keep latency under P95 targets.

Proposed next steps (owner / ETA):
- Redwood: spin up a Dedicated eval cluster and run 1k-record run using attached prompts (Owner: Monica) — target completion: 2028-07-25.
- Crestline: provide sanitized sample export (500–1k records) and confirm LegalOps artifact list (Owner: Julian) — target: 2028-07-22.
- Redwood + Crestline: 60-min technical deep-dive for schema edge-cases + retry behavior (Owners: Hannah + Julian) — proposed slots attached via Calendly link in-thread.

Open questions for the deep-dive:
- Are there any fields that must be strictly enumerated vs. free-text? (affects tokenization and cost)
- Acceptable fallback latency for degraded mode? (we proposed 5s max)

Attachment notes: sample prompts and the JSON schema are attached. Monica will follow with a short runbook for the eval tomorrow.

Thanks — Hannah

--

Thanks, Hannah — solid recap. A couple of clarifications before we hand off to our data team: 

1) Schema strictness: diagnosis_codes must map to ICD-11 codes only (enumerated). Summary can be free text up to 600 chars. Flags are boolean with a defined set.
2) Audit / security: can you confirm whether Dedicated supports HSM-backed KMS (we need to know for procurement)?

Also, can Monica call out what the failure-mode will look like in the response when the model returns non-conformant JSON? We need to ensure downstream services can retry vs. mark as 'requires-human-review'.

Great questions, Julian. Quick answers + attached test payload examples.

HSM / KMS: Dedicated supports customer KMS integrations; HSM-backed keys are available via our enterprise add-on (we can surface the integration checklist in the next 48 hours). I'll loop Security for a SOC 2 artifact copy you can attach to procurement.

Failure modes & suggested handling:
- Detection: Redwood structured-output validation returns a 422 + payload {"validation_errors": [ ... ]} when the model output fails to parse to the schema. We attach the raw model text in the response for debugging.
- Strategy:
  * If validation_errors.length <= 2 and confidence score >= 0.85, trigger an automatic retry with the same model and a stricter decoding setting (temperature 0.0, top_p 0.3).
  * If validation_errors > 2 OR confidence < 0.85, increment to fallback model (Mistral-Instruct-7B) and run with augmented prompt providing explicit field constraints.
  * If still failing, mark record for human review and flag in the audit log.

Retry matrix (attached in the runbook snippet):
- Attempt 1: model = Llama-3-13B-chat-q8, temp=0.0, max_tokens as needed, wait 200ms before next attempt if validation fails.
- Attempt 2: same model, more aggressive parsing hints in prompt, wait 400ms.
- Attempt 3: fallback to Mistral-Instruct-7B, temp=0.0, wait 800ms.
- Final: push to human-review queue and include full model trace.

Attachments included in this reply: small_test_payloads.json (50 records), schema_customer_response_v1.json (repeat), retry_matrix_v1.txt.

I'll start the Dedicated job tomorrow morning and post the first 200-run snapshot in the Drive link. If you can get us the sanitized sample export by Friday (2028-07-22), we'll aim to have the 1k run completed by next Tuesday.

Thanks — Monica
